title: Life stories

section_a.title: Zheng He, the great ancient Chinese explorer
paragraphs: In 1999, an American journalist reported a surprising encounter on a tiny African island called Pate, just off the coast of Kenya. There, in a village of stone huts set amongst dense trees, the journalist met a number of elderly men who told him that they were descendants of Chinese sailors, shipwrecked on Pate several centuries ago. Their ancestors had traded with the local Africans, who had given them giraffes to take back to China; then their boat was driven onto the nearby reef. He noted many clues that seemed to confirm the islanders’ tale, including their vaguely Asian appearance, the antique porcelain heirlooms in their homes, and the porcelain shards on the beaches. Evidently, this remote African village retains an echo of one of history’s most astonishing episodes of maritime exploration.

About six centuries ago, a mighty fleet of Chinese ships ventured west to the India Ocean, reaching Ceylon, Arabia, and East Africa. The fleet included giant nine-masted junks escorted by dozens of supply ships, water tankers, transports for cavalry horses, and patrol boats. The fleet’s crew totaled more than 27,000 sailors and soldiers. As a comparison, Columbus’ largest crew was of only about 1,500 people and the Santa Maria, the largest ship for his first voyage, was much smaller than Zheng He’s largest junk.

Seven times, from 1405 to 1433, the Chinese fleet set off for the unknown. These great expeditions took place about half a century before the first Europeans, rounding the tip of Africa in frail Portuguese caravels, “discovered” the Indian Ocean. The seven expeditions were all led by one man, Zheng He, one of the greatest explorers in Chinese history.

Zheng He was born around 1371 in Yunnan, southwestern China. As a child, he was very curious about the world. He often asked his father and grandfather, who had been to distant places, questions about their journey, along with the people and places they encountered. From a young age, he started reading books by great scholars, such as Confucius and Mencius. Later when he served in the royal court, he received military training and became a trusted assistant and adviser to the emperor. He was also in charge of palace construction and repairs, learned more about weapons, and became more knowledgeable in ship construction.

In 1403, the emperor commanded the construction of the Treasure Fleet. Both the treasure ships and the support vessels – battleships and boats carrying grain and horses – featured divided hulls with several watertight compartments. This engineering innovation had roots in early Chinese seafaring. It allowed mariners to take unprecedented amounts of drinking water on long voyages, while also adding much-needed ballast, balance, and stability.

In 1405, the emperor appointed Zheng He to head a massive fleet of more than 200 junks with a royal order to establish ties with rulers all around the Indian Ocean. It was the start of the seven great voyages of the Treasure Fleet. The junks, loaded with Chinese silk, porcelain, and lacquerware, visited ports around the Indian Ocean, where Zheng He exchanged the goods for spices, ivory, medicines, rare wood, pearls, and exotic animals, sought by the Ming court.

During his career as a naval commander, Zheng He negotiated trade pacts, fought pirates, and brought back gifts to China. He and his crew traveled and traded not only with the cities in what are now Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and India, but also with the Arabian ports of modern-day Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The rulers he encountered there were impressed by his diplomatic skills and the elaborate gifts he brought them. They agreed to send ambassadors to the Ming court.

In 1431, Zheng He set out with his fleet for the seventh expedition around the Indian Ocean, sailing all the way to Malindi on Kenya’s east coast and stopping at trading ports along the way. Toward the end of this voyage in 1433, Zheng He died of disease.

Zheng He had helped spread the culture and influence of China over a vast realm. But the war in the north then drew military investment away from the maintenance of the fleet and the royal court turned its focus to the construction and expansion of the Great Wall. Inevitably, the navy shrank and all the larger classes of ships were destroyed. This contributed to the end of the epic time of the Ming Dynasty sea voyages.

Zheng He spent years at sea sailing between China and the east coast of Africa, setting up diplomatic relationships that would reshape Asian life. His seven expeditions challenged what humans could do at sea, pushing the limits of their boats’ size, complexity, and capacity for long-distance travel. They were also essential to the spread of two Chinese technologies that helped build our modern world: gunpowder and the compass.

Today, whether people view Zheng He as an emblem of Chinese diplomacy or as a symbol of the country’s spirit of adventure and bravery, one thing is for certain: Zheng He remains one of the greatest explorers in world history, and the voyages he led stand among the great wonders in the history of ocean navigation, contributing significantly to the progress of human civilization.

section_b.title: Audrey Hepburn – a true angel in this world
paragraphs: Audrey Hepburn thrilled audiences with starring roles in noteworthy films like Breakfast at Tiffany’s, Sabrina, Roman Holiday, My Fair Lady, War and Peace, and Always.

Despite her success in the film domain, the roles she most preferred portraying were not in movies. She was an exemplary mother to her two sons and a UNICEF (the United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund) Goodwill Ambassador serving victims in war-torn countries.

As a young girl during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands, Audrey Hepburn was aware of the brutality, death, and destruction of war. She was malnourished, as her family was bankrupted as a result of the invasion. One day, Audrey was grabbed off the street by the Nazis and placed in line to be sent to a work camp. When the guards glanced away she darted off, barely escaping, and huddled in a cold, foul basement full of rats.

The little girl who would become one of the world’s most magical actresses began as an anonymous refugee confronting life’s horrors and fragility firsthand. She refused to allow her spirit to be afflicted by the desperate reality of her childhood. Instead, she transcended those challenges but never forgot what it felt like to suffer, to be hungry, alone, and helpless.

After the war, Audrey and her mother left the Netherlands and arrived in the U.K. Her dream of becoming a prime dancer drove her into a rigorous schedule at a famous ballet school. Later, she was spotted by a producer and eventually landed a role in the film Roman Holiday starring Gregory Peck, one of Hollywood’s top leading men.

Soon, Audrey was transformed from a malnourished girl into an internationally famous movie star. Director Billy Wilder complimented her, saying, “Audrey walked beautifully; she spoke beautifully.” Although she won many awards for acting, Audrey felt that her most significant work was humanitarian work for those in need, and as the mother to her two sons. She suffered through two divorces and from her memories of the war. Yet, Audrey never let her sadness overcome her or jeopardize her hope for a brighter future. Audrey finally met her soul mate, Robert Wolders, and spent the last 12 years of her life with him.

Becoming famous never changed Audrey’s generous and compassionate character. She felt a deep sense of responsibility to alleviate the suffering of those in need, especially children. Friends said Audrey had a complete lack of ego and accepted and appreciated others as they were.

Although she became very wealthy, she owned only one home in Switzerland. For Audrey it was a paradise where she could hide from the world with her beloved family, work in her garden, and take long walks in nature.

In 1988, Audrey was appointed a Goodwill Ambassador for UNICEF designed to provide emergency food and health care to children suffering as a result of war or other catastrophes. In that role, her lifelong passion for helping those in need found its greatest calling.

She turned down three million dollars to write her autobiography and instead accepted one dollar a year for the more conscientious role as an ambassador for UNICEF. For seven months out of each of her last five years, she and Robby left the peace and beauty in their cozy home to embark on outreach trips into some of the most difficult places on earth. From Bangladesh, Sudan, Vietnam, Kenya, Ethiopia, Central and South America, to Somalia, Audrey Hepburn traveled representing UNICEF, making over 50 emotionally draining and physically dangerous missions into bleak destinations to raise world awareness of wars and droughts. Having been a victim of war, she understood the blessing of being the beneficiary of food, clothing, and, most of all, hope.

Audrey felt it was wicked that billions of children were deprived of simple joys and drowned in overwhelming misery. She believed deeply in the ideology that all people share in the duty to care for those in need. Audrey was always ready to lead by example. She said, “When you deny childhood, you deny life.” She saw UNICEF’s work as an integral, sacred force in people’s lives and said of UNICEF’s results, “Anyone who doesn’t believe in miracles is not a realist.”
In 1992, Audrey was stricken by cancer. She, Robby, and her two sons returned to their home in Switzerland for their last Christmas together.

Audrey’s cherished friend, a world-famous fashion designer, spoke to her for the last time just before she died. He said she was “... serene at the end because she knew she had achieved everything with perfection”.
Audrey Hepburn’s passion for service was enduring. Even as her life ended at 63 years of age, she remained a gracious woman who perpetually signified simplicity, charity, charm, and kindness.

The majesty of Audrey Hepburn’s spirit of social responsibility and dedication lives on in her words: “Remember, if you ever need a helping hand, it’s at the end of your arm. As you get older, remember you have another hand: The first is to help yourself, the second is to help others.” And “For beautiful eyes, look for the good in others; for beautiful lips, speak only words of kindness; and for poise, walk with the knowledge that you are never alone.”

section_c.title: Mei Lanfang – a Peking Opera legend
paragraphs: Mei Lanfang, a Chinese theatrical performer, is recognized as one of the greatest Peking Opera artists in Chinese history. Actually, Mei Lanfang is his stage name and his real name is Mei Lan.

The son and grandson of noted opera singers, Mei began studying Peking Opera at the age of 8 and made his stage debut at 10, playing a weaving girl. Thereafter he played mostly female roles, becoming especially well-known for his portrayal in The Heavenly Maid Scatters Blossoms. At the age of 13 he joined the Xiliancheng Theatrical Company and, through performances in Shanghai and elsewhere, acquired a national reputation. His style of dance, singing, etc. won such acclaim over the years that it came to be known as the “Mei School”.

The early 1900s are widely considered the golden age of Peking Opera in China. Competition was fierce as opera troupes led by renowned stars toured all over China. Meanwhile, critics were ever ready to fire off their assessments of the quality of each troupe’s performance.

In a survey in 1927, the public voted for their favorite new play of the most famous Peking Opera performers of female roles. Such a role is known as dan. Among the performers were Mei Lanfang, Cheng Yanqiu, Shang Xiaoyun, and Xun Huisheng. Later, the four artists became widely known as the Four Great Dans of Peking Opera, and each went on to develop their own disciplines which have been studied and followed by generations of Peking Opera singers.

Mei was renowned for his efforts in modernizing Peking Opera in terms of plays, stage design, lighting, makeup, and costume design. Mei also made great contributions to the spread of Peking Opera to foreign countries by participating in cultural exchanges with Japan, the United States, and other countries. He toured the world, forming friendships with his Western contemporaries, including Charlie Chaplin.

During the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, Mei kept a moustache as a reply to the Japanese who asked him to perform. This bold act of patriotism earned him great respect and bolstered his fame as an artist.

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What did the elderly men on Pate tell the American journalist?
options: They were descendants of Chinese sailors shipwrecked on the island centuries before.
They had sailed to China on Zheng He’s fleet and decided to stay there.
They had bought Chinese porcelain from Portuguese traders.
They were the last survivors of a Chinese colony on the island.
questions.explanation: 第1段：老人告诉这位美国记者，他们是几百年前在帕泰岛失事的中国水手的后裔（descendants of Chinese sailors, shipwrecked on Pate several centuries ago）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What can be inferred from the comparison between the scale of Zheng He’s fleet and that of Columbus’?
options: Columbus’ voyage lasted much longer than Zheng He’s.
Both fleets carried about the same number of people.
Zheng He’s fleet was far larger and more powerful than Columbus’s.
Columbus had more ships but fewer soldiers than Zheng He.
questions.explanation: 第2段：郑和船队有27,000多名水手和士兵，而哥伦布最大的船员队伍只有约1,500人；郑和最大的宝船也比“圣玛丽亚号”大得多，可见其规模远超哥伦布。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why does the author use quotation marks around the word “discovered” (Para. 3)?
options: To show that the word is a direct quotation from an official record.
To suggest that Europeans were not really the first to reach the Indian Ocean.
To point out that the word is spelled wrongly in the original source.
To stress that the Indian Ocean was discovered by Asian sailors only.
questions.explanation: 第3段说这些远航比绕过好望角的第一批欧洲人早约半个世纪到达印度洋，引号带反讽意味：欧洲人并非真正“发现”了这片海域。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What kind of books did Zheng He start reading from a young age?
options: Books about the history of the Ming court.
Travel journals written by his father and grandfather.
Books by great scholars such as Confucius and Mencius.
questions.explanation: 第4段：他从小就开始读孔子、孟子等大学者的书（books by great scholars, such as Confucius and Mencius）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What order did Zheng He receive when he was appointed to head the massive fleet in 1405?
options: To build more than 200 new junks for the emperor.
To conquer the trading ports of the Arabian Peninsula.
To establish ties with rulers all around the Indian Ocean.
To bring back rare wood, pearls, and exotic animals.
questions.explanation: 第6段：皇帝命他率领两百多艘帆船的庞大船队，并下旨与印度洋周边的统治者建立联系（a royal order to establish ties with rulers all around the Indian Ocean）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How did Zheng He impress the rulers he encountered?
options: With his diplomatic skills and the elaborate gifts he brought.
With the size of his fleet and the number of his soldiers.
With his knowledge of the ports of Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
With the Chinese silk and porcelain he sold at low prices.
questions.explanation: 第7段：当地统治者对他的外交才能（diplomatic skills）和他带来的精美礼物印象深刻，并同意派使者到明朝。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why did the royal court draw military investment away from the maintenance of the Treasure Fleet?
options: Because pirates had destroyed most of the fleet.
Because Zheng He had died and no one could replace him.
Because the emperor wanted to spend the money on new trade pacts.
Because the war in the north led the court to focus on building and expanding the Great Wall.
questions.explanation: 第9段：北方的战争使军费不再用于船队维护，朝廷转而修建和扩建长城，海军随之萎缩，大型船只被毁。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is the influence of Zheng He’s seven expeditions on maritime exploration according to Para. 10?
options: They pushed the limits of boats’ size, complexity, and capacity for long-distance travel.
They proved that long-distance sea travel was too dangerous to continue.
They replaced gunpowder and the compass with new Chinese technologies.
They persuaded Asian rulers to stop trading across the Indian Ocean.
questions.explanation: 第10段：七次远航挑战了人类在海上能做到的事，把船只的规模、复杂程度和远距离航行能力推向极限，并传播了火药和指南针。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: The eastern area is three times bigger than the western area, featuring ______ tropical rainforests and giant waterfalls.
questions.explanation: dense 表示“茂密的”，dense tropical rainforests 即茂密的热带雨林，与 giant waterfalls 并列描写东部地区。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: In the meeting, a new manager was ______ to take charge of the project which was in financial difficulties.
questions.explanation: appoint sb. to do sth. 表示“任命某人做某事”，此处用被动 was appointed to take charge，说明新经理被任命接手项目。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Services such as cooking, cleaning, and ______ the elderly to hospitals are in high demand.
questions.explanation: escort sb. to somewhere 表示“护送某人去某地”，与 cooking、cleaning 并列作 Services 的内容，故用动名词 escorting。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: A high-tech police car capable of immediately detecting stolen cars, disqualified drivers, and other offenses is ______ the roads.
questions.explanation: patrol the roads 表示“在道路上巡逻”，主语是高科技警车，用现在分词 patrolling 构成现在进行时。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Around 300 workers and engineers are working hard for the timely delivery of the project despite its ______.
questions.explanation: despite its complexity 表示“尽管项目复杂”，complexity 指“复杂性”，符合 despite 后接名词的用法。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: A researcher said China’s fast economic ______ in recent years has made great contributions to world economic growth.
questions.explanation: economic expansion 表示“经济扩张（增长）”，与 in recent years 以及“对世界经济增长的贡献”搭配。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: That visit was hard work because he spoke no Chinese and had only a(n) ______ plan of action.
questions.explanation: a vague plan of action 表示“含糊的行动计划”，与前面“不会说中文”呼应，说明这次访问很艰难。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: China’s first domestically built polar icebreaker Xuelong 2 has completed its ______ period and will soon set out on a mission again.
questions.explanation: maintenance period 指船只的“维护保养期”，完成保养后才能再次出航执行任务。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: A number of people believe that genuine friendships can develop in both the digital and physical ______, with the boundaries between the two continuing to blur.
questions.explanation: in the digital and physical realm 表示“在数字领域和现实领域”，realm 指“（知识、活动、思想的）领域，范围”。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: She had to take care of the whole family, two children and two ______ elderly people, all by herself.
questions.explanation: frail elderly people 指“体弱的老人”，frail 表示“（尤指老人）瘦弱的、虚弱的”。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: I think it’ll be worthwhile to see what she did to overcome those problems and ______ the relations between the two countries, ending years of hostility.
questions.explanation: normalize the relations 表示“使两国关系正常化”，与 ending years of hostility（结束多年敌对）呼应。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: We are constantly acquiring new skills as we engage in activities or ______ ourselves with new devices.
questions.explanation: familiarize oneself with sth. 表示“使自己熟悉某物”，与 new devices 搭配。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: He described his boss as a(n) ______ who did not want to listen to other people’s advice.
questions.explanation: dictator 指“独裁者”，由 dictate + -or 构成，此处形容不听别人建议的老板。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: In their opinion, the production of things fundamental to life and human survival should not be ______.
questions.explanation: privatize 表示“使私有化”，此处用被动语态：关系民生的基本生产不应被私有化。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The insurance company sent a(n) ______ to look into the cause of the fire to see if it really was an accident.
questions.explanation: investigator 指“调查员”，由 investigate + -or 构成，负责调查火灾原因。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: One of the keys to the success of that company is its ability to ______ its services, which reduces the quality variance.
questions.explanation: standardize its services 表示“使服务标准化”，从而减少质量差异（quality variance）。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: His accomplishments as a composer have been recognized and widely ______ in the media.
questions.explanation: publicize 表示“宣传，使公开”，与 recognized and widely ... in the media 搭配。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Now we will ______ what we have learned and make a plan to improve our learning in the next semester or two.
questions.explanation: summarize what we have learned 表示“总结所学内容”，与后面的 make a plan 相承接。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Zheng He’s voyages, which aimed to promote trade and ______ with other states, lasted from 1405 to 1433.
questions.explanation: 词库 E diplomacy：promote trade and diplomacy 表示“促进贸易与外交”，与 with other states 搭配。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: He was talented in many ______, especially in ship construction.
questions.explanation: 词库 O realms：in many realms 表示“在许多领域”，后面用 especially in ship construction 具体说明。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: In 1403, the emperor ordered the construction of the Treasure Fleet and ______ Zheng He as the commander of this fleet.
questions.explanation: 词库 C appointed：appoint sb. as ... 表示“任命某人为……”。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: This began Zheng He’s ______ voyages, some of the most impressive exploration journeys in history.
questions.explanation: 词库 F epic：epic voyages 指“史诗般的航行”，与 some of the most impressive exploration journeys 呼应。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: They traded with the local people for spices, ivory, ______ animals, and other goods.
questions.explanation: 词库 G exotic：exotic animals 指“异国动物”，与 spices、ivory 并列作交换的货物。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: During the next six expeditions, Zheng He made trade ______ with the rulers of different states, brought back gifts, and established friendly relationships with them.
questions.explanation: 词库 N pacts：make trade pacts with sb. 表示“与某人订立贸易协定”。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: He even brought back with him ______ of various states to meet with the emperor of the Ming Dynasty.
questions.explanation: 词库 A ambassadors：bring back ambassadors 指把各国使者带回明朝觐见皇帝。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Zheng He’s seven great voyages promoted the ______ of China’s cultural and economic influence in the world.
questions.explanation: 词库 H expansion：the expansion of influence 表示“影响力的扩大”。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: He ______ new, friendly ties with many states on the Asian and African continents, while developing the trade relations with them.
questions.explanation: 词库 J forged：forge ties 表示“建立（牢固的）联系”。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Zheng He’s feat was unprecedented in the history of ocean ______.
questions.explanation: 词库 M navigation：ocean navigation 指“远洋航行”，与航海壮举呼应。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: We can enable our students to be ______ their own learning by creating interesting, open-ended tasks which they can finish by themselves.
questions.explanation: be in charge of their own learning 表示“对自己的学习负全责”，与后面“学生能独立完成的任务”呼应。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The festival, which falls on the ninth day of the ninth month on the lunar calendar, is ______ an occasion to pay respect to the elderly.
questions.explanation: be viewed as 表示“被视为”，此处说重阳节被视为敬老的日子。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The Belt and Road Initiative raises the level of connectivity and cooperation among dozens of nations that have ______ China for years.
questions.explanation: trade with China 表示“与中国贸易”，此处用现在完成时 have traded with。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: From the smallest birthday party to the largest concert, special events ______ every day in these parks.
questions.explanation: take place 表示“（尤指经过计划或安排后）发生、举行”，主语是 special events。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The train was fully ______ 50 containers of goods including glass bottles, canned food, and medical supplies.
questions.explanation: be loaded with 表示“装载着……”，与 50 containers of goods 搭配。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: Last month, the polar icebreaker ______ from the port for its new scientific expedition to the Antarctic.
questions.explanation: set off from the port 表示“从港口出发”，与 for its new scientific expedition 呼应。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: We have long been ______ what really goes on inside the space station and the video satisfied our curiosity.
questions.explanation: be curious about 表示“对……好奇”，与后面的 satisfied our curiosity 呼应。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: This is a double room and you can stay here ______ your friend.
questions.explanation: along with 表示“与……一起”，此处说可以和你的朋友一起住。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following did Audrey Hepburn prefer most?
options: Starring in as many films as possible.
questions.explanation: 第2段说她在电影之外最看重的是做两个儿子的模范母亲以及联合国儿童基金会亲善大使的工作；第6段又明确说她认为自己最有意义的工作是为需要帮助的人所做的人道主义工作。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding Audrey Hepburn’s life during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands?
options: Her mom managed to get her enough food.
She lived in a basement full of rats.
She failed to escape from the guards.
questions.explanation: 第3段：由于入侵，她的家庭破产（her family was bankrupted），她因此营养不良；她只是躲进满是老鼠的地下室，并非“住在”那里；她趁卫兵不注意逃走了。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn who experienced life’s horrors and fragility as a child?
options: She tried to forget the terrible experiences.
She was determined to overcome the challenges.
She lost hope at first but soon pulled herself together.
She did not admit that the desperate reality had an effect on her.
questions.explanation: 第4段：她不让自己的精神被童年的困境击垮，而是超越了这些挑战（she transcended those challenges），可见她决心战胜困难；同时她从未忘记受苦的滋味。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What happened to Audrey Hepburn after she moved to the U.K.?
options: She enrolled in a famous film school.
She met her soul mate Gregory Peck.
She wrote a biography of Billy Wilder.
She got a role in the film Roman Holiday.
questions.explanation: 第5段：她先进入著名芭蕾舞学校，后来被制片人发现，最终在《罗马假日》中获得角色；她的灵魂伴侣是 Robert Wolders，不是 Gregory Peck。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn’s home in Switzerland?
options: It was one of the several homes she owned.
It was very modern and life was comfortable there.
It was the place where she wrote her autobiography.
It was a place where she could stay with her family undisturbed.
questions.explanation: 第8段：她虽然富有，却只拥有一处住宅；对她来说那是可以“躲开世界”、与挚爱家人安静相处的乐园（a paradise where she could hide from the world with her beloved family）。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why does the author say Audrey’s missions were “physically dangerous”?
options: She went to remote places alone.
She visited places which were at war.
She had little time to rest during her missions.
She often encountered people hostile to foreigners.
questions.explanation: 第10段说她的出访地包括孟加拉国、苏丹、越南、埃塞俄比亚、索马里等正经历战争与旱灾的地方，因此这些人道主义行程在身体上很危险。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is the ideology Audrey Hepburn deeply believed in?
options: When you deny childhood, you deny life.
All people share in the duty to care for those in need.
Anyone who doesn’t believe in miracles is not a realist.
If you ever need a helping hand, it’s at the end of your arm.
questions.explanation: 第11段：她深信“所有人都分担着照顾需要帮助者的责任”这一理念（the ideology that all people share in the duty to care for those in need）。其余三项是她说过的话，不是“ideology”的内容。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: According to the text, which of the following words could best describe Audrey Hepburn?
questions.explanation: 全文反复写她慷慨、富有同情心、乐于助人（generous and compassionate, alleviate the suffering, gracious），kind-hearted 最能概括她的品格。

questions.heading: Reading skills
questions.question: Which of the following statements from Text B is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: After the war, Audrey and her mother left the Netherlands and arrived in the U.K.
In 1988, Audrey was appointed a Goodwill Ambassador for UNICEF.
Becoming famous never changed Audrey’s generous and compassionate character.
She, Robby, and her two sons returned to their home in Switzerland for their last Christmas together.
questions.explanation: 事实是可用时间、地点等核实的具体情况；C 句是对人物品格的评价（judgment），属于观点。A、B、D 都叙述了可核实的事件。

questions.heading: Reading skills
questions.question: Which of the following statements from Text B is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: Audrey was grabbed off the street by the Nazis and placed in line to be sent to a work camp.
Audrey walked beautifully; she spoke beautifully.
Even as her life ended at 63, she remained a gracious woman who perpetually signified simplicity, charity, charm, and kindness.
Audrey’s generosity and compassion made her one of the most admirable actresses in the world.
questions.explanation: A 句叙述可核实的具体事件（被纳粹抓走、排队送往劳动营），属于事实；其余各句含 beautiful、gracious、admirable 等主观评价词，属于观点。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Xu Xiake, a Chinese geographer and travel writer of the Ming Dynasty, traveled around China for over 30 years. In spite of many hardships and ______ dangerous situations along the way, he kept on traveling and left detailed and extensive records of his travels.
questions.explanation: physically dangerous 表示“在身体上危险的”，与 hardships 并列说明旅途艰险；emotionally 与 dangerous 不搭配。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: His writing, which ______ an echo of his love of nature, records numerous phenomena in the vast realm of nature and is widely admired for its high literary quality.
questions.explanation: retain an echo of 表示“保留着……的印迹/回声”；此处主语 His writing 为第三人称单数，故用 retains。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: His writing retains an echo of his love of nature and records numerous phenomena in the ______ realm of nature.
questions.explanation: the vast realm of nature 表示“广阔的自然领域”，vast 与 realm 搭配，也与前文“记录大量自然现象”呼应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: The vast trade network of the Silk Road carried more than just precious commodities. In fact, the constant movement and mixing of populations ______ different cultures and beliefs, which had a profound impact on the history and civilizations of the Eurasian peoples.
questions.explanation: spread different cultures and beliefs 表示“传播不同的文化与信仰”，与后文“对欧亚各民族历史与文明产生深远影响”一致。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Today travelers along the Silk Road are attracted not only by ______ gifts or local specialties, but also by surprising encounters with places with a mysterious past.
questions.explanation: elaborate gifts 表示“精美的礼物”，与 local specialties 并列，说明丝绸之路吸引游客的物品。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Today travelers along the Silk Road are attracted not only by elaborate gifts or local specialties, but also by ______ encounters with places with a mysterious past.
questions.explanation: surprising encounters 表示“令人惊喜的相遇”，与 a mysterious past 呼应；overwhelming／desperate 多修饰负面事物。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Charlie Chaplin may be one of the world’s most famous rags-to-riches actors. He lived in ______ misery when he was little.
questions.explanation: overwhelming misery 表示“铺天盖地的苦难”，overwhelming 常与 misery、despair 等词搭配。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Because of the ______ reality of poverty, he started to work when he was still a child.
questions.explanation: the desperate reality of poverty 表示“贫困的严酷现实”，desperate 修饰 reality 表示“令人绝望的”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: However, no hardship could ______ his hope, and he managed to overcome the obstacles and made a career out of making people laugh.
questions.explanation: jeopardize his hope 表示“危及他的希望”，与 no hardship could ... 以及 overcome the obstacles 呼应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Struggles and hardships happen to everyone in the ______ voyage of life, ordinary people and celebrities alike.
questions.explanation: the long voyage of life 表示“漫长的人生航程”，long 修饰 voyage，与“人人都会遇到挫折”呼应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: It is most important to get through the ______ draining periods in life by looking forward, drawing courage to face the odds, and hoping for the best.
questions.explanation: emotionally draining 表示“令人心力交瘁的”，与前文 personal setbacks、struggles 呼应，指情绪上的消耗。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: As a result, fears can never destroy your hope and determination. Finally you will achieve success which ______ signifies your devotion, efforts, and perseverance.
questions.explanation: perpetually signifies 表示“始终标志着”，perpetually 修饰 signifies，强调成功会一直印证你的付出与坚持。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: What was Mei Lanfang's real name?
questions.explanation: 第1段：梅兰芳是艺名，他的本名是梅兰（Mei Lan）。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: At what age did Mei Lanfang make his stage debut?
questions.explanation: 第2段：梅兰芳8岁学戏，10岁首次登台，扮演织女；13岁加入喜连成班社。题干问首次登台，故为10岁。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: Which of the following best shows Mei's contribution to spreading Peking Opera overseas?
options: He trained many foreign students in Beijing.
He wrote new plays about Western countries.
He performed only for foreign visitors at home.
He toured the world and met Western artists.
questions.explanation: 第5段：梅兰芳通过赴日本、美国等国的文化交流把京剧推向海外，还周游世界，与卓别林等西方同代艺术家结交。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: Why did Mei keep a moustache during the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression?
options: To follow an old tradition of the Mei School
To make himself look older on the stage
To refuse to perform for the Japanese
To protect his voice in cold weather
questions.explanation: 第6段：日方要求他演出时，梅兰芳蓄须明志，以示拒绝，这一爱国之举为他赢得极大尊重。

translation.zh: 中央电视台春节联欢晚会（Spring Festival Gala）自1983年举办以来，已成为中国人生活中不可缺少的文化消费品和一个重要的文化符号。
translation.en_reference: Since it was first staged in 1983, the CCTV Spring Festival Gala has become an indispensable cultural product in the life of the Chinese people and an important cultural symbol.

translation.zh: 虽然众口难调，但必须承认的是，“春晚”已成为一项“新民俗”。
translation.en_reference: It is hard to please everyone, but it must be admitted that the Gala has become a “new folk custom”.

translation.zh: 它不仅是一台晚会，更是一种仪式与象征，一种文化与标签，一种情感与寄托。
translation.en_reference: It is more than a gala: it is a ritual and a symbol, a culture and a label, a bond of emotion and a source of comfort.

translation.zh: 随着新媒体的出现，“春晚”也在与时俱进，以满足大众日渐多样化的需求。
translation.en_reference: With the rise of new media, the Gala has also kept pace with the times in order to meet the increasingly diverse needs of the public.

writing.prompt: Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics. One topic has an outline you can follow: an influential Chinese explorer. Develop your essay as a biographical narrative in chronological order, using time-order signals such as when, during, and later, and select only the details that best portray the person.
outline: When and where the explorer was born
How the explorer started his or her career
What the explorer has achieved and what contribution he or she has made to China and the world
Conclusion: the significance of the explorer to China and the world
